concepts.title: Mendel's Experiments and the Rules of Inheritance
concepts.definition: Gregor Mendel crossed pea plants with contrasting characters like tall and short: crossing pure tall with pure short gave all tall F1 plants, and self-pollinating them gave an F2 with three tall for every one short - proving traits are controlled by paired factors that separate and recombine.
concepts.key_idea: Three tall to one short: the 3 : 1 ratio exposed the hidden rules of inheritance.
concepts.textbook_ref: jesc108.txt sections on Mendel's monohybrid crosses

solution_steps.explain: Pure tall (TT) with pure short (tt) gives all Tt tall in F1.
Tt with Tt gives TT, Tt, Tt and tt in F2.

concepts.title: How Traits Are Expressed - Genes and DNA
concepts.definition: Chromosomes in the nucleus carry genes made of DNA; each gene pair controls a trait, enzymes made from gene instructions control plant height and other characters, and a changed gene - like the one for recessive shortness - changes the enzyme and hence the trait.
concepts.key_idea: Gene to enzyme to trait: DNA instructions express themselves through proteins.
concepts.textbook_ref: jesc108.txt sections on genes, DNA and expression of traits

solution_steps.explain: Genes sit on chromosomes inside the nucleus.
Gene instructs enzyme; enzyme decides the character.
One dominant gene masks the recessive partner's expression.

concepts.title: Sex Determination in Humans
concepts.definition: Human sex is decided at fertilisation by the sex chromosomes: females carry XX and males XY, so an egg with X meeting an X-sperm gives a girl and an X egg with a Y-sperm gives a boy - a 50 : 50 chance inherited from the father.
concepts.key_idea: The father's sperm decides: X or Y meets the mother's X - equal chances, no blame.
concepts.textbook_ref: jesc108.txt section on sex determination in humans
question_patterns: explain the sex determination mechanism in humans with a cross

solution_steps.explain: Mother is XX; father is XY.
All eggs carry X; sperms carry X or Y equally.
XX gives a girl and XY gives a boy, each with half probability.
